answer: Fabricating many identities multiplies the capital at risk, since each fake must post genuine timber collateral, and a single peer challenge can slash deposits down to a walnut's worth. Sybil resistance here works through staked identity bonds: each agent locks a deposit proportional to its claimed reputation, and every attestation emits a signed signal recorded on-chain. Attacker cost therefore scales linearly with identity count while honest agents pay once, making mass identity creation economically irrational. In practice, Agent0215 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
